input.content:
# Micro Intent API (v1)

This is the contract between the backend, the Chrome extension and the webapp.
Every part is built against this file in parallel, so keep it stable.
Any change to the contract must be documented here (see [Changelog](#changelog)) and called out in the PR description.

## Basics

- Base URL: `http://localhost:8080` locally, the Cloud Run service URL when deployed.
- All bodies are JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`), UTF-8.
- Times are ISO 8601 with offset, e.g. `2026-10-10T18:00:00+02:00`; the backend works in `Europe/Zurich`.
- CORS is open (`*`), so the extension (`chrome-extension://...`) and the webapp can call it directly.
- No auth in v1 (hackathon demo); one shared profile with id `default`.
- The Gemini key lives only in the backend; clients never see it (voice uses [ephemeral tokens](#post-voicetoken)).

## Endpoints at a glance

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST` | `/intent` | Page context + spoken/typed intent in, UI-spec card out. Never executes write actions. |
| `POST` | `/confirm` | Human approves (or rejects) one write action by id; only now is it executed. |
| `GET` | `/profile` | Read the user profile. |
| `PUT` | `/profile` | Update the user profile (partial merge). |
| `POST` | `/voice/token` | Short-lived Gemini Live token for voice input in the extension. |
| `GET` | `/health` | Liveness plus which sources are live or mocked. |
| `POST` | `/demo/reset` | Reset mock calendar, pending actions and reminders to the seeded demo state. |

## POST /intent

### Request

```json
{
  "intent": "Am I free, and how do I get there from Winterthur?",
  "context": {
    "url": "https://luma.com/example-event",
    "title": "{Tech: Europe} Agentic AI Hack Zurich - Luma",
    "selection": {
      "text": "Saturday, October 10 · 18:00 - 21:00 · Zurich",
      "element": {
        "tag": "div",
        "text": "Saturday, October 10 ...",
        "selector": "main > div.event-time",
        "attributes": { "aria-label": "Event time" }
      }
    },
    "gaze": {
      "text": "Saturday, October 10 · 18:00 - 21:00",
      "selector": "main > div.event-time",
      "x": 412,
      "y": 230,
      "dwell_ms": 900
    },
    "page_text": "Optional visible-text excerpt of the page, max 20000 chars."
  },
  "locale": "en",
  "now": "2026-10-10T14:00:00+02:00"
}
```

| Field | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `intent` | yes | What the user said or typed, verbatim. |
| `context.url` | yes | Page URL. |
| `context.title` | yes | `document.title`. |
| `context.selection` | no | What the user marked. `text` is the selected text; `element` describes the clicked/marked element when there is no text selection. |
| `context.gaze` | no | What the user looked at (eye tracking). Same shape as `selection.element` plus screen coordinates and dwell time. All fields optional. |
| `context.page_text` | no | Extra page text for grounding. Trimmed to 20000 chars server-side. |
| `locale` | no | `en` (default) or `de`. Card texts come back in this language. |
| `now` | no | Client clock; defaults to server time. Lets the demo pin "today". |

At least one of `selection`, `gaze` or `page_text` should be present; with none, the agent only sees URL and title.

### Response: UI-spec card

`/intent` always answers `200` with a card, including on internal errors (then `card_type: "error"`).
Only malformed requests get `422`.

```json
{
  "card_id": "card_7f3a2c",
  "card_type": "event_plan",
  "status": "conflict",
  "title": "Agentic AI Hack Zurich - Demo",
  "subtitle": "Sat 10 Oct · 18:00-21:00 · Zurich",
  "summary": "You have Team sync 18:00-18:30. The IC 5 at 17:02 from Winterthur gets you there by 17:28.",
  "speak": "You have a conflict with Team sync at six. The 17:02 IC from Winterthur gets you there in time.",
  "large_mode": false,
  "source": "agent",
  "sections": [
    {
      "type": "event",
      "title": "Agentic AI Hack Zurich - Demo",
      "start": "2026-10-10T18:00:00+02:00",
      "end": "2026-10-10T21:00:00+02:00",
      "location": "Zurich",
      "url": "https://luma.com/example-event"
    },
    {
      "type": "conflict",
      "title": "Team sync",
      "start": "2026-10-10T18:00:00+02:00",
      "end": "2026-10-10T18:30:00+02:00",
      "calendar": "Work"
    },
    {
      "type": "connections",
      "from": "Winterthur",
      "to": "Zürich HB",
      "items": [
        {
          "departure": "2026-10-10T17:02:00+02:00",
          "arrival": "2026-10-10T17:28:00+02:00",
          "duration_min": 26,
          "transfers": 0,
          "products": ["IC 5"],
          "platform": "4",
          "recommended": true
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "actions": [
    {
      "id": "act_9b1e04",
      "label": "Move Team sync to 17:00",
      "kind": "confirm",
      "style": "primary",
      "tool": "calendar_move",
      "preview": "Move \"Team sync\" from 18:00-18:30 to 17:00-17:30 on Sat 10 Oct.",
      "requires_confirmation": true
    },
    {
      "id": "act_c2d871",
      "label": "Add event + travel to calendar",
      "kind": "confirm",
      "style": "secondary",
      "tool": "calendar_create",
      "preview": "Create \"Agentic AI Hack Zurich - Demo\" 18:00-21:00 and \"Train IC 5 Winterthur → Zürich HB\" 17:02-17:28.",
      "requires_confirmation": true
    },
    {
      "id": "act_44aa10",
      "label": "Open SBB timetable",
      "kind": "open_url",
      "style": "secondary",
      "url": "https://www.sbb.ch/en?von=Winterthur&nach=Z%C3%BCrich%20HB",
      "requires_confirmation": false
    },
    {
      "id": "act_0d77e2",
      "label": "Dismiss",
      "kind": "dismiss",
      "style": "ghost",
      "requires_confirmation": false
    }
  ]
}
```

#### Card fields

| Field | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `card_id` | string | Unique per response. |
| `card_type` | enum | `event_plan`, `travel`, `calendar`, `reminder`, `message_draft`, `shared_slot`, `info`, `error`. Pick a layout/icon by it; all types use the same `sections` rendering. |
| `status` | enum | `ok`, `conflict`, `warning`, `error`. Drives the accent color. |
| `title` | string | Short headline. |
| `subtitle` | string? | One line under the title. |
| `summary` | string | One or two sentences answering the intent. Always present. |
| `speak` | string? | Shorter, speakable variant of `summary` for TTS. |
| `large_mode` | bool | Mirrors `profile.large_mode`: render bigger type, fewer sections, at most two actions visible. |
| `source` | enum | `agent` (Gemini answered live) or `fallback` (scripted demo path because a service failed). Show a subtle badge for `fallback`. |
| `sections` | array | Ordered content blocks, see below. Unknown `type`s must be ignored by clients. |
| `actions` | array | Ordered buttons, see below. |

#### Section types

All fields not marked required may be absent.

| `type` | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| `event` | `title`*, `start`*, `end`, `location`, `url` |
| `conflict` | `title`*, `start`*, `end`*, `calendar` |
| `free` | `text`* (e.g. "You are free 18:00-21:00.") |
| `connections` | `from`*, `to`*, `items`*: list of `{departure*, arrival*, duration_min, transfers, products[], platform, recommended}` |
| `slots` | `title`, `items`*: list of `{start*, end*, label}` (e.g. shared free slots) |
| `message` | `to`*: `{name*, relation, channel, address}`, `body`*, `editable` (bool; edits go back via `/confirm`) |
| `reminder` | `at`*, `text`* |
| `fields` | `items`*: list of `{label*, value*}` generic key-value rows |
| `text` | `text`* (plain text paragraph) |

#### Action kinds

| `kind` | Meaning | Client behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `confirm` | A write action (calendar create/move, reminder, send message). Always `requires_confirmation: true`. Nothing has happened yet. | Show `preview`, and only after an explicit user tap call `POST /confirm` with the `id`. |
| `open_url` | Open `url` in a new tab. | No backend call. |
| `followup` | Ask a follow-up. Carries `intent` (string). | Call `POST /intent` with this `intent` and the same `context`. |
| `dismiss` | Close the card. | No backend call. Optionally call `/confirm` with `approved: false` for pending confirm actions. |

Action fields: `id`* (unique, stable until confirmed or expired), `label`*, `kind`*, `style` (`primary` \| `secondary` \| `danger` \| `ghost`), `tool` (backend tool name for `confirm`), `preview` (human-readable effect, required for `confirm`), `requires_confirmation`* (bool), `url` (for `open_url`), `intent` (for `followup`), `expires_at` (pending confirm actions expire after 30 minutes).

## POST /confirm

The human checkpoint.
The backend executes a write action only through this endpoint, once per action id.

### Request

```json
{
  "action_id": "act_9b1e04",
  "approved": true,

# Micro Intent API (v1)

This is the contract between the backend, the Chrome extension and the webapp.
Every part is built against this file in parallel, so keep it stable.
Any change to the contract must be documented here (see [Changelog](#changelog)) and called out in the PR description.

## Basics

- Base URL: `http://localhost:8080` locally, the Cloud Run service URL when deployed.
- All bodies are JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`), UTF-8.
- Times are ISO 8601 with offset, e.g. `2026-10-10T18:00:00+02:00`; the backend works in `Europe/Zurich`.
- CORS is open (`*`), so the extension (`chrome-extension://...`) and the webapp can call it directly.
- No auth in v1 (hackathon demo); one shared profile with id `default`.
- The Gemini key lives only in the backend; clients never see it (voice uses [ephemeral tokens](#post-voicetoken)).

## Endpoints at a glance

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST` | `/intent` | Page context + spoken/typed intent in, UI-spec card out. Never executes write actions. |
| `POST` | `/confirm` | Human approves (or rejects) one write action by id; only now is it executed. |
| `GET` | `/profile` | Read the user profile. |
| `PUT` | `/profile` | Update the user profile (partial merge). |
| `POST` | `/voice/token` | Short-lived Gemini Live token for voice input in the extension. |
| `GET` | `/health` | Liveness plus which sources are live or mocked. |
| `POST` | `/demo/reset` | Reset mock calendar, pending actions and reminders to the seeded demo state. |

## POST /intent

### Request

```json
{
  "intent": "Am I free, and how do I get there from Winterthur?",
  "context": {
    "url": "https://luma.com/example-event",
    "title": "{Tech: Europe} Agentic AI Hack Zurich - Luma",
    "selection": {
      "text": "Saturday, October 10 · 18:00 - 21:00 · Zurich",
      "element": {
        "tag": "div",
        "text": "Saturday, October 10 ...",
        "selector": "main > div.event-time",
        "attributes": { "aria-label": "Event time" }
      }
    },
    "gaze": {
      "text": "Saturday, October 10 · 18:00 - 21:00",
      "selector": "main > div.event-time",
      "x": 412,
      "y": 230,
      "dwell_ms": 900
    },
    "page_text": "Optional visible-text excerpt of the page, max 20000 chars."
  },
  "locale": "en",
  "now": "2026-10-10T14:00:00+02:00"
}
```

| Field | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `intent` | yes | What the user said or typed, verbatim. |
| `context.url` | yes | Page URL. |
| `context.title` | yes | `document.title`. |
| `context.selection` | no | What the user marked. `text` is the selected text; `element` describes the clicked/marked element when there is no text selection. |
| `context.gaze` | no | What the user looked at (eye tracking). Same shape as `selection.element` plus screen coordinates and dwell time. All fields optional. |
| `context.page_text` | no | Extra page text for grounding. Trimmed to 20000 chars server-side. |
| `locale` | no | `en` (default) or `de`. Card texts come back in this language. |

Only malformed requests get `422`.

```json

  "card_id": "card_7f3a2c",
  "card_type": "event_plan",
  "status": "conflict",
  "title": "Agentic AI Hack Zurich - Demo",
  "subtitle": "Sat 10 Oct · 18:00-21:00 · Zurich",
  "summary": "You have Team sync 18:00-18:30. The IC 5 at 17:02 from Winterthur gets you there by 17:28.",
  "speak": "You have a conflict with Team sync at six. The 17:02 IC from Winterthur gets you there in time.",
  "large_mode": false,
  "source": "agent",
  "sections": [
    {
      "type": "event",
      "title": "Agentic AI Hack Zurich - Demo",
      "start": "2026-10-10T18:00:00+02:00",
      "end": "2026-10-10T21:00:00+02:00",
      "location": "Zurich",
      "url": "https://luma.com/example-event"
    },
    {
      "type": "conflict",
      "title": "Team sync",
      "start": "2026-10-10T18:00:00+02:00",
      "end": "2026-10-10T18:30:00+02:00",
      "calendar": "Work"
    },
    {
      "type": "connections",
      "from": "Winterthur",
      "to": "Zürich HB",
      "items": [
        {
          "departure": "2026-10-10T17:02:00+02:00",
          "arrival": "2026-10-10T17:28:00+02:00",
          "duration_min": 26,
          "transfers": 0,
          "products": ["IC 5"],
          "platform": "4",
          "recommended": true
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "actions": [
    {
      "id": "act_9b1e04",
      "label": "Move Team sync to 17:00",
      "kind": "confirm",
      "style": "primary",
      "tool": "calendar_move",
      "preview": "Move \"Team sync\" from 18:00-18:30 to 17:00-17:30 on Sat 10 Oct.",
      "requires_confirmation": true
    },

      "id": "act_c2d871",

      "kind": "confirm",
      "style": "secondary",
      "tool": "calendar_create",
      "preview": "Create \"Agentic AI Hack Zurich - Demo\" 18:00-21:00 and \"Train IC 5 Winterthur → Zürich HB\" 17:02-17:28.",
      "requires_confirmation": true
    },
    {
      "id": "act_44aa10",
      "label": "Open SBB timetable",
      "kind": "open_url",
      "style": "secondary",
      "url": "https://www.sbb.ch/en?von=Winterthur&nach=Z%C3%BCrich%20HB",
      "requires_confirmation": false
    },
    {
      "id": "act_0d77e2",
      "label": "Dismiss",
      "kind": "dismiss",
      "style": "ghost",
      "requires_confirmation": false
    }
  ]
}
```

#### Card fields

| Field | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `card_id` | string | Unique per response. |
| `card_type` | enum | `event_plan`, `travel`, `calendar`, `reminder`, `message_draft`, `shared_slot`, `info`, `error`. Pick a layout/icon by it; all types use the same `sections` rendering. |
| `status` | enum | `ok`, `conflict`, `warning`, `error`. Drives the accent color. |
| `title` | string | Short headline. |
| `subtitle` | string? | One line under the title. |
| `summary` | string | One or two sentences answering the intent. Always present. |
| `speak` | string? | Shorter, speakable variant of `summary` for TTS. |
| `large_mode` | bool | Mirrors `profile.large_mode`: render bigger type, fewer sections, at most two actions visible. |
| `source` | enum | `agent` (Gemini answered live) or `fallback` (scripted demo path because a service failed). Show a subtle badge for `fallback`. |
| `sections` | array | Ordered content blocks, see below. Unknown `type`s must be ignored by clients. |
| `actions` | array | Ordered buttons, see below. |

#### Section types

All fields not marked required may be absent.

| `type` | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| `event` | `title`*, `start`*, `end`, `location`, `url` |
| `conflict` | `title`*, `start`*, `end`*, `calendar` |
| `free` | `text`* (e.g. "You are free 18:00-21:00.") |
| `connections` | `from`*, `to`*, `items`*: list of `{departure*, arrival*, duration_min, transfers, products[], platform, recommended}` |
| `slots` | `title`, `items`*: list of `{start*, end*, label}` (e.g. shared free slots) |
| `message` | `to`*: `{name*, relation, channel, address}`, `body`*, `editable` (bool; edits go back via `/confirm`) |
| `reminder` | `at`*, `text`* |
| `fields` | `items`*: list of `{label*, value*}` generic key-value rows |
| `text` | `text`* (plain text paragraph) |

#### Action kinds

| `kind` | Meaning | Client behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `confirm` | A write action (calendar create/move, reminder, send message). Always `requires_confirmation: true`. Nothing has happened yet. | Show `preview`, and only after an explicit user tap call `POST /confirm` with the `id`. |
| `open_url` | Open `url` in a new tab. | No backend call. |
| `followup` | Ask a follow-up. Carries `intent` (string). | Call `POST /intent` with this `intent` and the same `context`. |
| `dismiss` | Close the card. | No backend call. Optionally call `/confirm` with `approved: false` for pending confirm actions. |

      "kind": "dismiss",
      "style": "ghost",
      "requires_confirmation": false
    }
  ]
}
```

#### Card fields

| Field | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `card_id` | string | Unique per response. |
| `card_type` | enum | `event_plan`, `travel`, `calendar`, `reminder`, `message_draft`, `shared_slot`, `info`, `error`. Pick a layout/icon by it; all types use the same `sections` rendering. |
| `status` | enum | `ok`, `conflict`, `warning`, `error`. Drives the accent color. |
| `title` | string | Short headline. |
| `subtitle` | string? | One line under the title. |
| `summary` | string | One or two sentences answering the intent. Always present. |
| `speak` | string? | Shorter, speakable variant of `summary` for TTS. |
| `large_mode` | bool | Mirrors `profile.large_mode`: render bigger type, fewer sections, at most two actions visible. |
| `source` | enum | `agent` (Gemini answered live) or `fallback` (scripted demo path because a service failed). Show a subtle badge for `fallback`. |
| `sections` | array | Ordered content blocks, see below. Unknown `type`s must be ignored by clients. |
| `actions` | array | Ordered buttons, see below. |

#### Section types

All fields not marked required may be absent.

| `type` | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| `event` | `title`*, `start`*, `end`, `location`, `url` |
| `conflict` | `title`*, `start`*, `end`*, `calendar` |
| `free` | `text`* (e.g. "You are free 18:00-21:00.") |
| `connections` | `from`*, `to`*, `items`*: list of `{departure*, arrival*, duration_min, transfers, products[], platform, recommended}` |
| `slots` | `title`, `items`*: list of `{start*, end*, label}` (e.g. shared free slots) |
| `message` | `to`*: `{name*, relation, channel, address}`, `body`*, `editable` (bool; edits go back via `/confirm`) |
| `reminder` | `at`*, `text`* |
| `fields` | `items`*: list of `{label*, value*}` generic key-value rows |
| `text` | `text`* (plain text paragraph) |

#### Action kinds

| `kind` | Meaning | Client behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `confirm` | A write action (calendar create/move, reminder, send message). Always `requires_confirmation: true`. Nothing has happened yet. | Show `preview`, and only after an explicit user tap call `POST /confirm` with the `id`. |
| `open_url` | Open `url` in a new tab. | No backend call. |
| `followup` | Ask a follow-up. Carries `intent` (string). | Call `POST /intent` with this `intent` and the same `context`. |
| `dismiss` | Close the card. | No backend call. Optionally call `/confirm` with `approved: false` for pending confirm actions. |

Action fields: `id`* (unique, stable until confirmed or expired), `label`*, `kind`*, `style` (`primary` \| `secondary` \| `danger` \| `ghost`), `tool` (backend tool name for `confirm`), `preview` (human-readable effect, required for `confirm`), `requires_confirmation`* (bool), `url` (for `open_url`), `intent` (for `followup`), `expires_at` (pending confirm actions expire after 30 minutes).

## POST /confirm

The human checkpoint.
The backend executes a write action only through this endpoint, once per action id.

### Request

```json
{
  "action_id": "act_9b1e04",
  "approved": true,
  "edits": { "body": "Hi Mom, I'll be home around 22:30." }
}
```

| Field | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `action_id` | yes | `id` of a `confirm` action from an `/intent` card. |
| `approved` | no | Default `true`. `false` cancels the pending action (nothing is executed). |
| `edits` | no | User edits before approval. Supported: `body` for message drafts, `start`/`end` for calendar actions, `text`/`at` for reminders. |

### Response

```json
{
  "action_id": "act_9b1e04",
  "status": "done",
  "message": "Moved \"Team sync\" to 17:00-17:30.",
  "result": { "event_id": "evt_team_sync", "start": "2026-10-10T17:00:00+02:00", "end": "2026-10-10T17:30:00+02:00" },
  "card": { "card_id": "card_...", "card_type": "calendar", "status": "ok", "title": "Done", "summary": "Moved \"Team sync\" to 17:00-17:30.", "sections": [], "actions": [] }
}
```

| `status` | HTTP | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `done` | 200 | Executed. `result` holds tool output, `card` is a small result card to render in place. |
| `rejected` | 200 | `approved: false`; nothing executed. |
| `failed` | 200 | Execution failed; `message` says why. The action stays pending and may be retried. |
| `already_done` | 200 | This id was already executed; nothing executed again. |
| `not_found` | 404 | Unknown or expired id. |

## GET /profile

```json
{
  "name": "Batu",
  "home": "Winterthur",
  "transport": "public",
  "contacts": [
    { "id": "mom", "name": "Mom", "relation": "mother", "channel": "sms", "address": "+41790000000" }
  ],
  "large_mode": false,
  "locale": "en"
}
```

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | Display name. |
| `home` | Home town or station, used as default origin for travel ("from home"). |
| `transport` | `public` (default), `car`, `bike`, `walk`. Only `public` gets live connections in v1. |
| `contacts` | People the agent may draft messages to ("tell my mom"). `channel`: `sms`, `whatsapp`, `email`. |
| `large_mode` | Accessibility mode: large type, fewer choices. Echoed on every card. |
| `locale` | Default card language (`en` or `de`). |

## PUT /profile

Partial merge: send only the fields to change; omitted fields keep their value.
`contacts`, when sent, replaces the whole list.
Returns the full updated profile (same shape as `GET /profile`).

```json
{ "home": "Winterthur", "large_mode": true }
```

## POST /voice/token

Mints a short-lived, single-use Gemini Live auth token so the extension can stream microphone audio straight to Gemini Live without holding the API key.

Request body: `{}` (optional `{ "locale": "de" }`).

```json
{
  "token": "auth_tokens/abc123...",
  "model": "gemini-3.8-live",
  "api_version": "v1alpha",
  "expires_at": "2026-10-10T14:30:00Z",
  "new_session_expires_at": "2026-10-10T14:01:00Z"
}
```

Client usage (JS SDK `@google/genai`):

```js
const { token, model, api_version } = await (await fetch(`${API}/voice/token`, { method: "POST", headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: "{}" })).json();
const ai = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: token, httpOptions: { apiVersion: api_version } });
const session = await ai.live.connect({ model, config: { responseModalities: ["TEXT"], inputAudioTranscription: {} }, callbacks: { /* ... */ } });
```

The token allows one session start within about a minute (`new_session_expires_at`) and that session may run until `expires_at`.
Use the input transcription as the `intent` for `POST /intent`.
Returns `503` with `{ "detail": "..." }` if the backend has no Gemini key; the client should then fall back to typed input or the Web Speech API.

## GET /health

```json
{ "ok": true, "version": "0.1.0", "model": "gemini-3.8-flash", "calendar": "mock", "gemini": true, "force_fallback": false }
```

## POST /demo/reset

Resets the mock calendar (back to the planted "Team sync 18:00-18:30" conflict), drops pending actions, reminders and sent messages.
Returns `{ "ok": true }`.
Call it before each demo run.

## Errors

- `422`: request validation failed (FastAPI default body: `{ "detail": [...] }`).
- `404`: unknown resource (e.g. action id).
- `503`: a required backend secret is missing (voice token only).
- `/intent` never returns `5xx` for agent or upstream failures; it returns a `fallback` or `error` card instead.

## Changelog

- v1 (2026-10-10): initial contract.

"""Process-local state: profile, pending (unconfirmed) write actions, reminders and the message outbox.

Cloud Run must run a single instance (see deploy.sh) so a /confirm hits the instance that issued the action.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
import threading
import uuid
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from .config import settings
from .models import Contact, Profile, ProfileUpdate

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

ACTION_TTL = timedelta(minutes=30)


def new_id(prefix: str) -> str:
    return f"{prefix}_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"


def default_profile() -> Profile:
    return Profile(
        name="Batu",
        home="Winterthur",
        transport="public",
        contacts=[
            Contact(id="mom", name="Mom", relation="mother", channel="sms", address="+41790000000"),
            Contact(id="anna", name="Anna", relation="teammate", channel="email", address="anna@example.com"),
        ],
        large_mode=False,
        locale="en",
    )


@dataclass
class PendingAction:
    id: str
    tool: str
    label: str
    preview: str
    ops: list[dict[str, Any]]
    expires_at: datetime
    status: str = "pending"
    result: dict[str, Any] | None = None


@dataclass
class Store:

"""Gemini agent on the Interactions API with function calling; ends with a render_card call."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
from typing import Any

from google import genai

from .compose import finalize
from .config import settings
from .models import Card, IntentRequest
from .tools import TOOL_DECLARATIONS, RequestCtx, call_tool

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

MAX_ROUNDS = 6
PAGE_TEXT_LIMIT = 20000

SYSTEM = """You are Micro Intent, an agent inside the user's browser.
The user looked at or selected something on a web page and said what they want.
You act with tools and answer with ONE UI card (render_card), never with chat prose.

Rules:
- Ground everything in the page context and tool results; never invent times, trains or calendar entries.
- For events on the page: extract title, start, end and location (resolve relative dates like "Today" against NOW).
- "Am I free" means: call calendar_free_busy for the event window.
- "How do I get there" means: call sbb_connections from the user's origin (stated origin, else profile.home) to the event location (use the town or main station, e.g. "Zürich HB" for Zurich) arriving about 10 minutes before the start, with is_arrival_time=true. If the event already started, travel from NOW with is_arrival_time=false.
- Call independent read tools in parallel in the same turn.
- Writes (calendar_create, calendar_move, set_reminder, draft_message) are only PROPOSALS that the human approves later. Propose the helpful ones:
  - a calendar conflict: propose calendar_move of the conflicting event to a free slot earlier the same day (check with calendar_free_busy), keeping its duration;
  - an event the user wants to attend: propose calendar_create for the event and, if travelling, a separate calendar_create for the recommended train;
  - "tell/notify <contact>": draft_message with a short, warm first-person text.
- Never say an action was done; say what you propose. Keep summary to 1-2 short sentences.
- Finish with exactly one render_card call. Use status "conflict" when the user is busy during the event.
- Write card texts in the requested locale."""


def _client() -> genai.Client:
    return genai.Client(api_key=settings.gemini_api_key)


def _user_input(req: IntentRequest, ctx: RequestCtx) -> str:
    context = req.context.model_dump(exclude_none=True)
    if context.get("page_text"):
        context["page_text"] = context["page_text"][:PAGE_TEXT_LIMIT]
    payload = {
        "intent": req.intent,
        "page": context,
        "now": ctx.now.isoformat(),
        "timezone": str(settings.tz),
        "locale": ctx.locale,
        "profile": ctx.profile.model_dump(),
    }
    return json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False)


def _step_dict(step: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return step.model_dump(mode="json", exclude_none=True) if hasattr(step, "model_dump") else dict(step)


def run_agent(req: IntentRequest, ctx: RequestCtx) -> Card:
    client = _client()
    common = {
        "model": settings.model,
        "system_instruction": SYSTEM,
        "tools": TOOL_DECLARATIONS,
        "generation_config": {"thinking_level": "low", "temperature": 0.2},
        "store": True,
    }
    interaction = client.interactions.create(input=_user_input(req, ctx), **common)
    for _ in range(MAX_ROUNDS):
        steps = [_step_dict(s) for s in (interaction.steps or [])]
        calls = [s for s in steps if s.get("type") == "function_call"]
        render = next((c for c in calls if c["name"] == "render_card"), None)
        results = []
        for call in calls:
            if call["name"] == "render_card":
                continue
            out = call_tool(ctx, call["name"], call.get("arguments") or {})
            log.info("tool %s(%s) -> %s", call["name"], json.dumps(call.get("arguments"), ensure_ascii=False)[:300], json.dumps(out, ensure_ascii=False)[:300])
            results.append({"type": "function_result", "call_id": call["id"], "name": call["name"], "result": json.dumps(out, ensure_ascii=False)})
        if render is not None:
            return _card_from_render(ctx, render.get("arguments") or {})
        if not calls:
            text = (interaction.output_text or "").strip()
            if not text:
                raise RuntimeError(f"agent ended without a card (status={interaction.status})")
            return finalize(ctx, card_type="info", status="ok", title=req.context.title[:60], summary=text, source="agent")
        interaction = client.interactions.create(input=results, previous_interaction_id=interaction.id, **common)
    raise RuntimeError("agent exceeded max rounds")


def _card_from_render(ctx: RequestCtx, args: dict[str, Any]) -> Card:
    return finalize(
        ctx,
        card_type=args.get("card_type", "info"),
        status=args.get("status", "ok"),
        title=args.get("title") or "Micro Intent",
        subtitle=args.get("subtitle"),
        summary=args.get("summary") or "",
        speak=args.get("speak"),
        event=args.get("event"),
        notes=args.get("notes"),
        followups=args.get("followups"),
        source="agent",
    )

"""Ephemeral Gemini Live tokens, so the extension never holds the API key."""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

from google import genai
from google.genai import types

from .config import settings

API_VERSION = "v1alpha"


def mint_live_token() -> dict:
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    expires = now + timedelta(minutes=30)
    new_session_expires = now + timedelta(minutes=1)
    client = genai.Client(api_key=settings.gemini_api_key, http_options={"api_version": API_VERSION})
    token = client.auth_tokens.create(
        config=types.CreateAuthTokenConfig(
            uses=1,
            expire_time=expires,
            new_session_expire_time=new_session_expires,
            # Lock only the model; the client chooses its own session config.
            live_constrained_parameters=types.LiveEphemeralParameters(model=settings.live_model),
            lock_additional_fields=[],
        )
    )
    return {
        "token": token.name,
        "model": settings.live_model,
        "api_version": API_VERSION,
        "expires_at": expires.isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z"),
        "new_session_expires_at": new_session_expires.isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z"),
    }

The page you provided doesn't include the v0.9 message types, JSON field names, or example JSON, so I can't give you those from it. It only links to the specs:

- **v0.9 A2UI Protocol:** `specification/v0.9-a2ui/`
- **v0.9 Evolution Guide:** `specification/v0.9-evolution-guide/`

These are relative links on the A2UI docs site, and the page doesn't show the base URL. The source repository is at `github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui`, and the page has a "View source" link for the index page at `docs/public/index.md`.

The page does say that v0.9 is the "Previous Stable" version and that it:

}

## Envelope message structure The envelope defines four primary message types, and every message streamed by the server must be a JSON object containing exactly one of the following keys: `createSurface`, `updateComponents`, `updateDataModel`, or `deleteSurface`. The key indicates the type of message, and these are the messages that make up each message in the protocol stream. ### `createSurface` This message signals the client to create a new surface and begin rendering it. A surface must be created before any `updateComponents` or `updateDataModel` messages can be sent to it. While typically achieved by the agent sending a `createSurface` message, an agent may skip this if it knows the surface has already been created (e.g., by another agent). Once a surface is created, its `surfaceId` and `catalogId` are fixed; to reconfigure them, the surface must be deleted and recreated. It is an error to send `createSurface` for a `surfaceId` that already exists without first deleting it. One of the components in one of the component lists MUST have an `id` of `root` to serve as the root of the component tree. **Properties:** - `surfaceId` (string, required): The unique identifier for the UI surface to be rendered. - `catalogId` (string, required): A string that uniquely identifies the catalog (components and functions) used for this surface. Note that `catalogId` is a string identifier, not a resolvable URI; while it is conventionally formatted as a URI (e.g., `https://mycompany.com/1.0/somecatalog`) to avoid naming collisions across organizations, it does not need to point to any deployed resource or downloadable file. Client and server developers must agree on shared catalogs with well-known IDs in order to build systems that are compatible with each other. - `theme` (object, optional): A JSON object containing theme parameters (e.g., `primaryColor`) defined in the catalog's theme schema. - `sendDataModel` (boolean, optional): If true, the client will send the full data model of this surface in the metadata of every message sent to the server (via the Transport's metadata mechanism). This ensures the surface owner receives the full current state of the UI alongside the user's action or query. Defaults to false. **Example:** ```json { "version": "v0.9.1", "createSurface": { "surfaceId": "user_profile_card", "catalogId": "https://a2ui.org/specification/v0_9_1/catalogs/basic/catalog.json", "theme": { "primaryColor": "#00BFFF" }, "sendDataModel": true } } ``` ### `updateComponents` This message provides a list of UI components to be added to or updated within a specific surface. The components are provided as a flat list, and their relationships are defined by ID references in an adjacency list. This message may only be sent to a surface that has already been created. Note that components may reference children or data bindings that do not yet exist; clients should handle this gracefully by rendering placeholders (progressive rendering). **Properties:** - `surfaceId` (string, required): The unique identifier for the UI surface to be updated. This is typically a name with meaning (e.g. "user_profile_card"), and it has to be unique within the context of the GenUI session. - `components` (array, required): A list of component objects. The components are provided as a flat list, and their relationships are defined by ID references in an adjacency list. **Example:** ```json { "version": "v0.9.1", "updateComponents": { "surfaceId": "user_profile_card", "components": [ { "id": "root", "component": "Column", "children": ["user_name", "user_title"] }, { "id": "user_name", "component": "Text", "text": "John Doe" }, { "id": "user_title", "component": "Text", "text": "Software Engineer" } ] } } ``` ### `updateDataModel` This message is used to send or update the data that populates the UI components. It allows the server to change the UI's content without resending the entire component structure. The `updateDataModel` message replaces the value at the specified `path` with the new content. If `path` is omitted (or is `/`), the entire data model for the surface is replaced. **Properties:** - `surfaceId` (string, required): The unique identifier for the UI surface this data model update applies to. - `path` (string, optional): A JSON Pointer to the location in the data model to update. Defaults to `/`. - `value` (any, optional): The new value for the specified path. If omitted, the key at `path` is removed. **Example:** ```json { "version": "v0.9.1", "updateDataModel": { "surfaceId": "user_profile_card", "path": "/user/name", "value": "Jane Doe" } } ``` ### `deleteSurface` This message instructs the client to remove a surface and all its associated components and data from the UI. **Properties:** - `surfaceId` (string, required): The unique identifier for the UI surface to be deleted. **Example:** ```json { "version": "v0.9.1", "deleteSurface": { "surfaceId": "user_profile_card" } } ``` ## Example Stream The following example demonstrates a complete interaction to render a Contact Form, expressed as a JSONL stream. ```jsonl {"version": "v0.9.1", "createSurface":{"surfaceId":"contact_form_1","catalogId":"https://a2ui.org/specification/v0_9_1/catalogs/basic/catalog.json"}} {"version": "v0.9.1", "updateComponents":{"surfaceId":"contact_form_1","components":[{"id":"root","component":"Card","child":"form_container"},{"id":"form_container","component":"Column","children":["header_row","name_row","email_group","phone_group","pref_group","divider_1","newsletter_checkbox","submit_button"],"justify":"start","align":"stretch"},{"id":"header_row","component":"Row","children":["header_icon","header_text"],"align":"center"},{"id":"header_icon","component":"Icon","name":"mail"},{"id":"header_text","component":"Text","text":"# Contact Us","variant":"h2"},{"id":"name_row","component":"Row","children":["first_name_group","last_name_group"],"justify":"spaceBetween"},{"id":"first_name_group","component":"Column","children":["first_name_label","first_name_field"],"weight":1},{"id":"first_name_label","component":"Text","text":"First Name","variant":"caption"},{"id":"first_name_field","component":"TextField","label":"First Name","value":{"path":"/contact/firstName"},"variant":"shortText"},{"id":"last_name_group","component":"Column","children":["last_name_label","last_name_field"],"weight":1},{"id":"last_name_label","component":"Text","text":"Last Name","variant":"caption"},{"id":"last_name_field","component":"TextField","label":"Last Name","value":{"path":"/contact/lastName"},"variant":"shortText"},{"id":"email_group","component":"Column","children":["email_label","email_field"]},{"id":"email_label","component":"Text","text":"Email Address","variant":"caption"},{"id":"email_field","component":"TextField","label":"Email","value":{"path":"/contact/email"},"variant":"shortText","checks":[{"call":"required","args":{"value":{"path":"/contact/email"}},"message":"Email number must be 10 digits."}]},{"id":"pref_group","component":"Column","children":["pref_label","pref_picker"]},{"id":"pref_label","component":"Text","text":"Preferred Contact Method","variant":"caption"},{"id":"pref_picker","component":"ChoicePicker","variant":"mutuallyExclusive","options":[{"label":"Email","value":"email"},{"label":"Phone","value":"phone"},{"label":"SMS","value":"sms"}],"value":{"path":"/contact/preference"}},{"id":"divider_1","component":"Divider","axis":"horizontal"},{"id":"newsletter_checkbox","component":"CheckBox","label":"Subscribe {"version": "v0.9.1", "deleteSurface":{"surfaceId":"contact_form_1"}} ``` ## Component model A2UI's component model is designed for flexibility, separating the protocol's structure from the set of available UI components. ### The component object Each object in the `components` array of an `updateComponents` message defines a single UI component. It has the following structure: - `id` (`ComponentId`, required): A unique string that identifies this specific component instance. This is used for parent-child references. - `component` (string, required): Specifies the component's type (e.g., `"Text"`). - **Component Properties**: Other properties relevant to the specific component type (e.g., `text`, `url`, `children`) are included directly in the component object. This structure is designed to be both flexible and strictly validated. ### The component catalog The set of available UI components and functions is defined in a **Catalog**. The basic catalog is defined in [`catalogs/basic/catalog.json`]. While the Basic Catalog is useful for starting out, most production applications will define their own catalog to reflect their specific design system. The server must generate messages that conform to the catalog understood by the client. #### Catalog Identification & Compatibility Each catalog is identified by a `catalogId` string. The `catalogId` is a string identifier used for matching catalogs between the client and server. While it is conventional to format catalog IDs as URIs (e.g., `https://mycompany.com/catalogs/v1`) to prevent naming collisions across organizations, a `catalogId` is not required to be a resolvable network resource. Because A2UI catalogs are represented as JSON Schema documents, catalog definitions should include both `$id` (used by JSON Schema tooling) and `catalogId` (used by A2UI SDKs and catalog negotiation), and both fields should be set to the same URI. It is up to client and server developers to agree on shared catalogs with well-known IDs in order to build systems that are compatible with each other. ### UI composition: the adjacency list model The A2UI protocol defines the UI as a flat list of components. The tree structure is built implicitly using ID references. This is known as an adjacency list model. Container components (like `Row`, `Column`, `List`, and `Card`) have properties that reference the `id` of their child component(s). The client is responsible for storing all components in a map (e.g., `Map`) and recreating the tree structure at render time. This model allows the server to send component definitions in any order. Rendering can begin as soon as the `root` component is defined, with the client filling in or updating the rest of the tree progressively as additional definitions arrive. There must be exactly one component with the ID `root` in the component tree, acting as the root of the component tree. Until that component is defined, other component updates will have no visible effect, and they will be buffered until a root component is defined. Once a root component is defined, the client is responsible for rendering the tree in the best way possible based on the available data, skipping invalid references. ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph "Server Stream" A("updateComponents
components: [root, title, button]") end subgraph "Client-Side Buffer (Map)" C("root: {id: 'root', component: 'Column', children: ['title', 'button']}") D("title: {id: 'title', component: 'Text', text: 'Welcome'}") E("button: {id: 'button', component: 'Button', child: 'button_label'}") end subgraph "Rendered Widget Tree" F(Column) --> G(Text: 'Welcome') F --> H(Button) end A -- "Parsed and stored" --> C A -- "Parsed and stored" --> D A -- "Parsed and stored" --> E ``` ### Defining actions Interactive components (like `Button`) use an `action` property to define what happens when the user interacts with them. Actions can either trigger an event sent to the server or execute a local client-side function. #### Server actions To send an event to the server, use the `event` property within the `action` object. It requires a `name` and an optional `context`. ```json { "component": "Button", "text": "Submit", "action": { "event": { "name": "submit_form", "context": { "itemId": "123" } } } } ``` #### Local actions To execute a local function, use the `functionCall` property within the `action` object. This property references a standard `FunctionCall` object. ```json { "component": "Button", "text": "Open Link", "action": { "functionCall": { "call": "openUrl", "args": { "url": "${/url}" } } } } ``` ## Data model representation: binding, scope This section describes how UI components **represent** and reference data from the Data Model. A2UI relies on a strictly defined relationship between the UI structure (Components) and the state (Data Model), defining the mechanics of path resolution, variable scope during iteration. ### Path resolution & scope ## Client-to-server messages The protocol also defines messages that the client can send to the server, which are defined in the [`client_to_server.json`] schema. These are used for handling user interactions and reporting client-side information. ### `action` This message is sent when the user interacts with a component that has an `action` defined, such as a `Button`. **Properties:** - `name` (string, required): The name of the action. - `surfaceId` (string, required): The ID of the surface where the action originated. - `sourceComponentId` (string, required): The ID of the component that triggered the action. - `timestamp` (string, required): An ISO 8601 timestamp. - `context` (object, required): A JSON object containing any context provided in the component's `action` property. ### Capabilities & metadata In A2UI v0.9, capabilities and other metadata are exchanged via **Transport metadata** or initialization payloads (e.g., A2A metadata, Agent Cards, or MCP initialization), rather than as first-class A2UI messages. #### Server capabilities A server (or agent) advertises its capabilities using the [`server_capabilities.json`] schema. This indicates which catalogs it can generate UI for, and whether it accepts inline catalogs from the client. The exact mechanism depends on the transport (e.g., the `params` object in an A2A AgentCard, or server capabilities in MCP). #### Client capabilities The `a2uiClientCapabilities` object in the A2A `Message`'s `metadata` field follows the [`client_capabilities.json`] schema. **Properties:** - `supportedCatalogIds` (array of strings, required): String identifiers of supported catalogs. - `inlineCatalogs`: An array of inline catalog definitions provided directly by the client (useful for custom or ad-hoc components and functions). #### Client data model When `sendDataModel` is enabled for a surface, the client includes the `a2uiClientDataModel` object in the metadata, following the [`client_data_model.json`] schema. **Properties:** - `surfaces` (object, required): A map of surface IDs to their current data models. ### `error` This message is used to report a client-side error to the server. [`catalogs/basic/catalog.json`]: ../catalogs/basic/catalog.json [`common_types.json`]: ../json/common_types.json [`server_to_client.json`]: ../json/server_to_client.json [`client_to_server.json`]: ../json/client_to_server.json [`server_capabilities.json`]: ../json/server_capabilities.json [`client_capabilities.json`]: ../json/client_capabilities.json [`client_data_model.json`]: ../json/client_data_model.json [JSON Pointer]: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6901 [RFC 6901]: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6901

Actions can either trigger an event sent to the server or execute a local client-side function. #### Server actions To send an event to the server, use the `event` property within the `action` object. It requires a `name` and an optional `context`. ```json { "component": "Button", "text": "Submit", "action": { "event": { "name": "submit_form", "context": { "itemId": "123" } } } } ``` #### Local actions To execute a local function, use the `functionCall` property within the `action` object. This property references a standard `FunctionCall` object. ```json { "component": "Button", "text": "Open Link", "action": { "functionCall": { "call": "openUrl", "args": { "url": "${/url}" } } } } ``` ## Data model representation: binding, scope This section describes how UI components **represent** and reference data from the Data Model. A2UI relies on a strictly defined relationship between the UI structure (Components) and the state (Data Model), defining the mechanics of path resolution, variable scope during iteration. ### Path resolution & scope ## Client-to-server messages The protocol also defines messages that the client can send to the server, which are defined in the [`client_to_server.json`] schema. These are used for handling user interactions and reporting client-side information. ### `action` This message is sent when the user interacts with a component that has an `action` defined, such as a `Button`. **Properties:** - `name` (string, required): The name of the action. - `surfaceId` (string, required): The ID of the surface where the action originated. - `sourceComponentId` (string, required): The ID of the component that triggered the action. - `timestamp` (string, required): An ISO 8601 timestamp. - `context` (object, required): A JSON object containing any context provided in the component's `action` property. ### Capabilities & metadata In A2UI v0.9, capabilities and other metadata are exchanged via **Transport metadata** or initialization payloads (e.g., A2A metadata, Agent Cards, or MCP initialization), rather than as first-class A2UI messages. #### Server capabilities A server (or agent) advertises its capabilities using the [`server_capabilities.json`] schema. This indicates which catalogs it can generate UI for, and whether it accepts inline catalogs from the client. The exact mechanism depends on the transport (e.g., the `params` object in an A2A AgentCard, or server capabilities in MCP). #### Client capabilities The `a2uiClientCapabilities` object in the A2A `Message`'s `metadata` field follows the [`client_capabilities.json`] schema. **Properties:** - `supportedCatalogIds` (array of strings, required): String identifiers of supported catalogs. - `inlineCatalogs`: An array of inline catalog definitions provided directly by the client (useful for custom or ad-hoc components and functions). #### Client data model When `sendDataModel` is enabled for a surface, the client includes the `a2uiClientDataModel` object in the metadata, following the [`client_data_model.json`] schema. **Properties:** - `surfaces` (object, required): A map of surface IDs to their current data models. ### `error` This message is used to report a client-side error to the server. input.content:
# Micro Intent API (v1)

This is the contract between the backend, the client shell (Chrome extension or desktop app) and the webapp.
Every part is built against this file in parallel, so keep it stable.
Any change to the contract must be documented here (see [Changelog](#changelog)) and called out in the PR description.

## Basics

- Base URL: `http://localhost:8080` locally, the Cloud Run service URL when deployed.
- All bodies are JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`), UTF-8.
- Times are ISO 8601 with offset, e.g. `2026-10-10T18:00:00+02:00`; the backend works in `Europe/Zurich`.
- CORS is open (`*`), so any client shell and the webapp can call it directly.
- No auth in v1 (hackathon demo); one shared profile.
- The Gemini key lives only in the backend; clients never see it (voice uses [ephemeral tokens](#post-voicetoken)).
- Page and screen content is untrusted input: the agent treats it as data, never as instructions, and stays read-only until the user confirms an action.

## Generative UI: A2UI v0.9.1

Cards are [A2UI](https://a2ui.org) v0.9.1 server-to-client messages (`createSurface`, `updateComponents`, `updateDataModel`, `deleteSurface`, each with `"version": "v0.9.1"`).
The agent never emits free-form UI: it only picks components from the trusted client catalog below, and the backend fills them with data from its tools.
The client renders them with a React A2UI renderer that registers this catalog.

- `catalogId`: `https://micro-intent.app/a2ui/catalog/v1` (an identifier, not a resolvable URL).
- One card = one surface; the root component of every surface has `id: "root"` and is one of the catalog components.
- Buttons inside components are A2UI actions (`{"event": {"name": ..., "context": {...}}}` for the backend, `{"functionCall": {"call": "openUrl", ...}}` for local ones).
- When the user taps a server action, the client sends the standard A2UI client-to-server `action` message to [`POST /action`](#post-action).

### The turn contract

Every agent turn ends with one internal tool call `respond(say, cards)`; the backend never parses model free text.
Each turn response has the same shape, whether from `/intent`, `/intent/stream` or `/action`:

```json
{
  "turn_id": "turn_3f9a1c",
  "say": "Heads up: Team sync overlaps at six. The 17:31 IC 8 gets you there by 17:57.",
  "source": "agent",
  "cards": [
    { "version": "v0.9.1", "createSurface": { "surfaceId": "turn_3f9a1c_event", "catalogId": "https://micro-intent.app/a2ui/catalog/v1" } },
    { "version": "v0.9.1", "updateComponents": { "surfaceId": "turn_3f9a1c_event", "components": [ { "id": "root", "component": "EventCard", "...": "..." } ] } }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `turn_id` | Unique per turn; prefixes all surface ids of the turn. |
| `say` | One short spoken line. The client speaks it (TTS) and shows the Orb in `speaking` state meanwhile. Always present. |
| `source` | `agent` (Gemini answered live) or `fallback` (scripted path because Gemini or a service failed). Show a subtle badge for `fallback`. |
| `cards` | Flat list of A2UI v0.9.1 messages, in order. Feed them to the A2UI message processor as-is. May be empty. |

### Catalog `https://micro-intent.app/a2ui/catalog/v1`

Props marked * are always present.
Action props are A2UI `Action` objects; the backend sets their `context`, so the client only forwards it.

#### Orb

Client-driven assistant indicator (package `thinking-orbs` from libraries.dev/orbs).
The backend does not send Orb surfaces in v1; the client drives the state from the turn lifecycle and the [stream events](#post-intentstream).

| Prop | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `state`* | `idle`, `listening`, `thinking`, `searching`, `speaking`. |

#### EventCard

The event the user looked at, with availability.

| Prop | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `title`* | Event title. |
| `start`*, `end` | ISO times. |
| `location`, `url` | Optional. |
| `availability`* | `free`, `conflict` or `unknown`. |
| `addAction` | Optional confirm action: add the event (and the recommended train) to the calendar. Carries `preview`. |

#### ConflictCard

A calendar entry that overlaps the event, with three choices: move, skip, keep.

| Prop | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `conflict`* | `{ "eventId", "title", "start", "end", "calendar" }`. |
| `eventTitle`* | The event it collides with. |
| `move` | `{ "label", "preview", "newStart", "newEnd", "action" }` - proposal to move the conflicting entry to a free slot; `action` is a confirm action. Absent if no free slot was found. |
| `skipAction`* | Skip the new event (nothing is written). |
| `keepAction`* | Keep both as they are (nothing is written). |

#### TrainCard

Public transport connections (SBB).

| Prop | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `from`*, `to`* | Station names. |
| `connections`* | List of `{ "departure", "arrival", "durationMin", "transfers", "products": ["IC 8"], "platform", "recommended" }`, at most 4. |
| `live`* | `true` for live SBB data, `false` for the scripted timetable fallback. |
| `openAction`* | Local action `{"functionCall": {"call": "openUrl", "args": {"url": "..."}}}` to the route. |

#### ReminderCard

| Prop | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `text`*, `at`* | Reminder text and time. |
| `preview`* | What will be written. |
| `confirmAction`*, `rejectAction`* | Server actions. |

#### MessageDraftCard

A message to a contact (e.g. notify family), only a draft until approved.
The body is editable through the data model: the surface's data model holds `/draft/body`, the text field binds to it, and `sendAction` sends the edited body back.

| Prop | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `to`* | `{ "name", "relation", "channel" }`; `channel` is `sms`, `whatsapp` or `email`. |
| `body`* | `{ "path": "/draft/body" }` (A2UI data binding). |
| `preview`* | What will be sent. |
| `sendAction`*, `discardAction`* | Server actions; `sendAction.event.context.body` is bound to `/draft/body`. |

#### ConfirmCard

Generic human checkpoint for any other write action (e.g. create calendar entries).

| Prop | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `title`* | Short label, e.g. "Add to calendar". |
| `preview`* | Exactly what will be written. |
| `tool`* | Backend tool, e.g. `calendar_create`. |
| `confirmAction`*, `rejectAction`* | Server actions. |

#### Server action names

| `event.name` | Meaning | `context` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `confirm` | Human approves a write action; only now is it executed. | `action_id`*, optional edits (`body`, `start`, `end`, `text`, `at`). |
| `reject` | Human declines a write action; nothing is executed. | `action_id`*. |
| `skip` | ConflictCard: skip the new event. | `action_id` of the move proposal (rejected). |
| `keep` | ConflictCard: keep both. | `action_id` of the move proposal (rejected). |

### Example: demo turn

Intent "Am I free, and how do I get there from Winterthur?" on the hackathon's Luma page (abridged):

```json
{
  "turn_id": "turn_3f9a1c",
  "say": "Heads up: Team sync overlaps at six. The 17:31 IC 8 from Winterthur gets you there by 17:57.",
  "source": "agent",
  "cards": [
    { "version": "v0.9.1", "createSurface": { "surfaceId": "turn_3f9a1c_conflict", "catalogId": "https://micro-intent.app/a2ui/catalog/v1" } },
    { "version": "v0.9.1", "updateComponents": { "surfaceId": "turn_3f9a1c_conflict", "components": [ {
      "id": "root",
      "component": "ConflictCard",
      "conflict": { "eventId": "evt_team_sync_20261010", "title": "Team sync", "start": "2026-10-10T18:00:00+02:00", "end": "2026-10-10T18:30:00+02:00", "calendar": "Work" },
      "eventTitle": "Agentic AI Hack Zurich",
      "move": {
        "label": "Move Team sync to 16:30",
        "preview": "Move \"Team sync\" from 18:00-18:30 to 16:30-17:00 on Sat 10 Oct.",
        "newStart": "2026-10-10T16:30:00+02:00",
        "newEnd": "2026-10-10T17:00:00+02:00",
        "action": { "event": { "name": "confirm", "context": { "action_id": "act_9b1e04" } } }
      },
      "skipAction": { "event": { "name": "skip", "context": { "action_id": "act_9b1e04" } } },
      "keepAction": { "event": { "name": "keep", "context": { "action_id": "act_9b1e04" } } }
    } ] } },
    { "version": "v0.9.1", "createSurface": { "surfaceId": "turn_3f9a1c_train", "catalogId": "https://micro-intent.app/a2ui/catalog/v1" } },
    { "version": "v0.9.1", "updateComponents": { "surfaceId": "turn_3f9a1c_train", "components": [ {
      "id": "root",
      "component": "TrainCard",
      "from": "Winterthur",
      "to": "Zürich HB",
      "live": true,
      "connections": [
        { "departure": "2026-10-10T17:31:00+02:00", "arrival": "2026-10-10T17:57:00+02:00", "durationMin": 26, "transfers": 0, "products": ["IC 8"], "platform": "4", "recommended": true }
      ],
      "openAction": { "functionCall": { "call": "openUrl", "args": { "url": "https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&origin=Winterthur&destination=Z%C3%BCrich+HB&travelmode=transit" } } }
    } ] } }
  ]
}
```

## Endpoints at a glance

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST` | `/intent` | Page context + intent in, one turn (`say` + A2UI `cards`) out. Never executes write actions. |
| `POST` | `/intent/stream` | Same, as Server-Sent Events with orb states and a filler line while tools run. |
| `POST` | `/action` | A2UI client-to-server `action` message (confirm / reject / skip / keep). The human checkpoint. |
| `POST` | `/confirm` | Shorthand for `/action` with a plain `{ "action_id", "approved", "edits" }` body. |
| `GET` | `/profile` | Read the user profile. |
| `PUT` | `/profile` | Update the user profile (partial merge). |
| `POST` | `/voice/token` | Short-lived Gemini Live token for voice input. |
| `GET` | `/health` | Liveness plus which sources are live or mocked. |
| `POST` | `/demo/reset` | Reset mock calendar, pending actions and reminders to the seeded demo state. |

## POST /intent

### Request

```json
{
  "intent": "Am I free, and how do I get there from Winterthur?",
  "context": {
    "url": "https://luma.com/example-event",
    "title": "{Tech: Europe} Agentic AI Hack Zurich - Luma",
    "selection": {
      "text": "Saturday, October 10 · 18:00 - 21:00 · Zurich",
      "element": { "tag": "div", "text": "Saturday, October 10 ...", "selector": "main > div.event-time", "attributes": { "aria-label": "Event time" } }
    },
    "gaze": { "text": "Saturday, October 10 · 18:00 - 21:00", "selector": "main > div.event-time", "x": 412, "y": 230, "dwell_ms": 900 },
    "page_text": "Optional visible-text excerpt of the page or screen, max 20000 chars."
  },

  "now": "2026-10-10T14:00:00+02:00"
}

| Field | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `intent` | yes | What the user said or typed, verbatim. |
| `context.url` | yes | Page URL (or app/window name in a desktop shell). |
| `context.title` | yes | Page or window title. |
| `context.selection` | no | What the user marked. `text` is the selected text; `element` describes the marked element when there is no text selection. |
| `context.gaze` | no | What the user looked at (eye tracking). All fields optional. |
| `context.page_text` | no | Extra page/screen text for grounding. Trimmed to 20000 chars server-side. |
| `locale` | no | `en` (default from profile) or `de`. `say` and card texts come back in this language. |
| `now` | no | Client clock; defaults to server time. Lets the demo pin "today". |

### Response

A [turn](#the-turn-contract).
`/intent` always answers `200` with a turn, including on internal errors (then a fallback or error turn).
Only malformed requests get `422`.

## POST /intent/stream

Same request as `/intent`; the response is `text/event-stream` with these events (each `data:` is JSON):

| `event:` | `data` | Client behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `orb` | `{ "state": "thinking" \| "searching" }` | Set the Orb state. |
| `filler` | `{ "say": "Checking your calendar and trains..." }` | Speak/show the filler line while tools run. |
| `turn` | A full [turn](#the-turn-contract). | Render `cards`, speak `say`, Orb to `speaking`. Last event. |

Order: `orb thinking` → `filler` → `orb searching` → `turn`.
Use it from `fetch` with a streaming reader (EventSource cannot POST).

## POST /action

The human checkpoint.
The backend executes a write action only through this endpoint (or `/confirm`), once per action id.

### Request: A2UI v0.9.1 client-to-server message

```json
{
  "version": "v0.9.1",
  "action": {
    "name": "confirm",
    "surfaceId": "turn_3f9a1c_conflict",
    "sourceComponentId": "root",
    "timestamp": "2026-10-10T14:00:12Z",
    "context": { "action_id": "act_9b1e04" }
  }
}
```

### Response

A [turn](#the-turn-contract) plus the outcome:

```json
{
  "turn_id": "turn_77d0b2",
  "say": "Done. Team sync is now at 16:30.",
  "source": "agent",
  "cards": [
    { "version": "v0.9.1", "deleteSurface": { "surfaceId": "turn_3f9a1c_conflict" } }
  ],
  "action_id": "act_9b1e04",
  "status": "done",
  "message": "Moved \"Team sync\" to 16:30-17:00.",
  "result": { "event": { "id": "evt_team_sync_20261010", "title": "Team sync", "start": "2026-10-10T16:30:00+02:00", "end": "2026-10-10T17:00:00+02:00" } }
}
```

| `status` | HTTP | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `done` | 200 | Executed; the surface that carried the action is deleted (`deleteSurface`). For `draft_message`, `result.message_sent.deep_link` is an `sms:`/`wa.me`/`mailto:` link the client may open to actually send. |
| `rejected` | 200 | `reject`, `skip` or `keep`; nothing executed; the surface is deleted. |
| `failed` | 200 | Execution failed; `message` says why. The action stays pending and may be retried. |
| `already_done` | 200 | This id was already handled; nothing executed again. |
| `not_found` | 404 | Unknown or expired id (pending actions expire after 30 minutes). |

## POST /confirm

Shorthand for clients without an A2UI action message at hand; same response as `/action`.

```json
{ "action_id": "act_9b1e04", "approved": true, "edits": { "body": "Hi Mom, I'll be home around 22:30." } }
```

`approved: false` equals `reject`.

## GET /profile

```json
{
  "name": "Batu",
  "home": "Winterthur",
  "transport": "public",
  "contacts": [
    { "id": "mom", "name": "Mom", "relation": "mother", "channel": "sms", "address": "+41790000000" }
  ],
  "large_mode": false,
  "locale": "en"
}
```

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | Display name. |
| `home` | Home town or station, used as default origin for travel ("from home"). |
| `transport` | `public` (default), `car`, `bike`, `walk`. Only `public` gets live connections in v1. |
| `contacts` | People the agent may draft messages to ("tell my mom"). `channel`: `sms`, `whatsapp`, `email`. |
| `large_mode` | Accessibility mode: the client renders large type and fewer choices. |
| `locale` | Default language (`en` or `de`). |

## PUT /profile

Partial merge: send only the fields to change; omitted fields keep their value.
`contacts`, when sent, replaces the whole list.
Returns the full updated profile (same shape as `GET /profile`).

```json
{ "home": "Winterthur", "large_mode": true }
```

## POST /voice/token

Voice sits behind one client-side interface so the provider can change (Gemini Live now, Gradium STT/TTS possible).
This endpoint serves the Gemini Live provider: it mints a short-lived, single-use auth token so the client streams microphone audio straight to Gemini Live without holding the API key.

Request body: `{}` (optional `{ "locale": "de" }`).

```json
{
  "provider": "gemini-live",
  "token": "auth_tokens/abc123...",
  "model": "gemini-3.8-live",
  "api_version": "v1alpha",
  "expires_at": "2026-10-10T14:30:00Z",
  "new_session_expires_at": "2026-10-10T14:01:00Z"
}
```

Client usage (JS SDK `@google/genai`):

```js
const { token, model, api_version } = await (await fetch(`${API}/voice/token`, { method: "POST", headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: "{}" })).json();
const ai = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: token, httpOptions: { apiVersion: api_version } });
const session = await ai.live.connect({ model, config: { responseModalities: ["TEXT"], inputAudioTranscription: {} }, callbacks: { /* ... */ } });
```

The token allows one session start within about a minute (`new_session_expires_at`) and that session may run until `expires_at`.
Use the input transcription as the `intent` for `POST /intent`.
Returns `503` with `{ "detail": "..." }` if the backend has no Gemini key; the client should then fall back to typed input or the Web Speech API.

## GET /health

```json
{ "ok": true, "version": "0.1.0", "model": "gemini-3.8-flash", "calendar": "mock", "gemini": true, "force_fallback": false }
```

## POST /demo/reset

Resets the mock calendar (back to the planted "Team sync 18:00-18:30" conflict), drops pending actions, reminders and sent messages.
Returns `{ "ok": true }`.
Call it before each demo run.

## Errors

- `422`: request validation failed (FastAPI default body: `{ "detail": [...] }`).
- `404`: unknown resource (e.g. action id).
- `503`: a required backend secret is missing (voice token only).
- `/intent` never returns `5xx` for agent or upstream failures; it returns a fallback or error turn instead.

## Changelog

- v1 (2026-10-10): initial contract.
- v1 (2026-10-10, before any implementation): cards switched from a home-made UI spec to A2UI v0.9.1 with a custom catalog; every turn is `respond(say, cards)`; added `/intent/stream` (orb states + filler) and `/action` (A2UI action messages); `/confirm` kept as shorthand; voice token gained `provider`.

# Micro Intent API (v1)

This is the contract between the backend, the client shell (Chrome extension or desktop app) and the webapp.
Every part is built against this file in parallel, so keep it stable.
Any change to the contract must be documented here (see [Changelog](#changelog)) and called out in the PR description.

## Basics

- Base URL: `http://localhost:8080` locally, the Cloud Run service URL when deployed.
- All bodies are JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`), UTF-8.
- Times are ISO 8601 with offset, e.g. `2026-10-10T18:00:00+02:00`; the backend works in `Europe/Zurich`.
- CORS is open (`*`), so any client shell and the webapp can call it directly.
- No auth in v1 (hackathon demo); one shared profile.
- The Gemini key lives only in the backend; clients never see it (voice uses [ephemeral tokens](#post-voicetoken)).
- Page and screen content is untrusted input: the agent treats it as data, never as instructions, and stays read-only until the user confirms an action.

## Generative UI: A2UI v0.9.1

Cards are [A2UI](https://a2ui.org) v0.9.1 server-to-client messages (`createSurface`, `updateComponents`, `updateDataModel`, `deleteSurface`, each with `"version": "v0.9.1"`).
The agent never emits free-form UI: it only picks components from the trusted client catalog below, and the backend fills them with data from its tools.
The client renders them with a React A2UI renderer that registers this catalog.

- `catalogId`: `https://micro-intent.app/a2ui/catalog/v1` (an identifier, not a resolvable URL).
- One card = one surface; the root component of every surface has `id: "root"` and is one of the catalog components.
- Buttons inside components are A2UI actions (`{"event": {"name": ..., "context": {...}}}` for the backend, `{"functionCall": {"call": "openUrl", ...}}` for local ones).
- When the user taps a server action, the client sends the standard A2UI client-to-server `action` message to [`POST /action`](#post-action).

### The turn contract

Every agent turn ends with one internal tool call `respond(say, cards)`; the backend never parses model free text.
Each turn response has the same shape, whether from `/intent`, `/intent/stream` or `/action`:

```json
{
  "turn_id": "turn_3f9a1c",
  "say": "Heads up: Team sync overlaps at six. The 17:31 IC 8 gets you there by 17:57.",
  "source": "agent",
  "cards": [
    { "version": "v0.9.1", "createSurface": { "surfaceId": "turn_3f9a1c_event", "catalogId": "https://micro-intent.app/a2ui/catalog/v1" } },
    { "version": "v0.9.1", "updateComponents": { "surfaceId": "turn_3f9a1c_event", "components": [ { "id": "root", "component": "EventCard", "...": "..." } ] } }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `turn_id` | Unique per turn; prefixes all surface ids of the turn. |
| `say` | One short spoken line. The client speaks it (TTS) and shows the Orb in `speaking` state meanwhile. Always present. |
| `source` | `agent` (Gemini answered live) or `fallback` (scripted path because Gemini or a service failed). Show a subtle badge for `fallback`. |
| `cards` | Flat list of A2UI v0.9.1 messages, in order. Feed them to the A2UI message processor as-is. May be empty. |

### Catalog `https://micro-intent.app/a2ui/catalog/v1`

Props marked * are always present.
Action props are A2UI `Action` objects; the backend sets their `context`, so the client only forwards it.

#### Orb

Client-driven assistant indicator (package `thinking-orbs` from libraries.dev/orbs).
The backend does not send Orb surfaces in v1; the client drives the state from the turn lifecycle and the [stream events](#post-intentstream).

| Prop | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `state`* | `idle`, `listening`, `thinking`, `searching`, `speaking`. |

#### EventCard

The event the user looked at, with availability.

| Prop | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `title`* | Event title. |
| `start`*, `end` | ISO times. |
| `location`, `url` | Optional. |
| `availability`* | `free`, `conflict` or `unknown`. |
| `addAction` | Optional confirm action: add the event (and the recommended train) to the calendar. Carries `preview`. |

#### ConflictCard

A calendar entry that overlaps the event, with three choices: move, skip, keep.

| Prop | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `conflict`* | `{ "eventId", "title", "start", "end", "calendar" }`. |
| `eventTitle`* | The event it collides with. |
| `move` | `{ "label", "preview", "newStart", "newEnd", "action" }` - proposal to move the conflicting entry to a free slot; `action` is a confirm action. Absent if no free slot was found. |
| `skipAction`* | Skip the new event (nothing is written). |
| `keepAction`* | Keep both as they are (nothing is written). |

#### TrainCard

Public transport connections (SBB).

| Prop | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `from`*, `to`* | Station names. |
| `connections`* | List of `{ "departure", "arrival", "durationMin", "transfers", "products": ["IC 8"], "platform", "recommended" }`, at most 4. |
| `live`* | `true` for live SBB data, `false` for the scripted timetable fallback. |
| `openAction`* | Local action `{"functionCall": {"call": "openUrl", "args": {"url": "..."}}}` to the route. |

#### ReminderCard

| Prop | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `text`*, `at`* | Reminder text and time. |
| `preview`* | What will be written. |
| `confirmAction`*, `rejectAction`* | Server actions. |

#### MessageDraftCard

A message to a contact (e.g. notify family), only a draft until approved.
The body is editable through the data model: the surface's data model holds `/draft/body`, the text field binds to it, and `sendAction` sends the edited body back.

| Prop | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `to`* | `{ "name", "relation", "channel" }`; `channel` is `sms`, `whatsapp` or `email`. |
| `body`* | `{ "path": "/draft/body" }` (A2UI data binding). |
| `preview`* | What will be sent. |
| `sendAction`*, `discardAction`* | Server actions; `sendAction.event.context.body` is bound to `/draft/body`. |

#### ConfirmCard

Generic human checkpoint for any other write action (e.g. create calendar entries).

| Prop | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `title`* | Short label, e.g. "Add to calendar". |
| `preview`* | Exactly what will be written. |
| `tool`* | Backend tool, e.g. `calendar_create`. |
| `confirmAction`*, `rejectAction`* | Server actions. |

#### Server action names

| `event.name` | Meaning | `context` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `confirm` | Human approves a write action; only now is it executed. | `action_id`*, optional edits (`body`, `start`, `end`, `text`, `at`). |
| `reject` | Human declines a write action; nothing is executed. | `action_id`*. |
| `skip` | ConflictCard: skip the new event. | `action_id` of the move proposal (rejected). |
| `keep` | ConflictCard: keep both. | `action_id` of the move proposal (rejected). |

### Example: demo turn

Intent "Am I free, and how do I get there from Winterthur?" on the hackathon's Luma page (abridged):
